references.text: The preceding verse describes the first brother who took the woman as his wife and died childless, and verse 30 continues with the second brother doing the same, in accordance with the law of levirate marriage ([ref:Luk 20:29|Luke 20:29]).
Verse 31 continues the sequence with the third brother and finally all seven, who all died without leaving any children ([ref:Luk 20:31|Luke 20:31]).
The parallel passage in Mark tells the same about the second brother who took the woman as his wife and died without leaving offspring ([ref:Mark 12:21|Mark 12:21]).
The parallel passage in Matthew describes how the second brother likewise took her as his wife and died ([ref:Matt 22:26|Matthew 22:26]).

The law of levirate marriage (levirate) that underlies this entire story: the deceased's brother shall take his widow as his wife and raise up offspring for his brother ([ref:5 Mos 25:5-6|Deuteronomy 25:5-6]).
